findings.oracle: Real ProcessBridge enumeration drives the tab; the row for os.getpid() must render the genuine image name (== Path(sys.executable).name, contains 'python') and a thread count cross-checked against psutil.Process(os.getpid()).num_threads(); replaces the len>=2/all(pid>=0) weak checks so a hardcoded/stale snapshot diverges and fails.

Separates magnitude from label: asserts rendered rows>10 and >= len(psutil.pids())//4 (real OS scale, not a single injected row) and os.getpid() present, then asserts the label text == f'{rows} processes'; a single hand-set row or stale binding now fails.

findings.ref: tests/test_bridges/test_plugin_deploy.py:file-level - fake DUMMY_PE headers / weak deploy assertion
findings.oracle: Replaces b'MZ'+nulls stubs with programmatically built spec-valid PEs (correct IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE AMD64 for .dp64, I386 for .dp32); after deploy, _assert_deployed_pe verifies SHA-256 byte-identity source-vs-target AND pefile parses the deployed file with the matching machine type plus MZ/PE signatures, so an arch-cross or byte-corruption fails (falsifiability confirmed).

Parametrized over step_into/step_over/step_out/run/pause/stop: asserts the bridge's real error-classification contract on the unavailable-plugin path - ToolError.tool_name=='x64dbg', details['x64dbg_error_code']=='plugin_unavailable', and details['command']==the originating method name - not merely 'raises ToolError'; mislabelled command, wrong code, swallowed fault, or a returned value fail the gate.
